a3430.speech: Reaffirmed the ministry's commitment to sustaining the country's immunisation programmes despite increasing budgetary pressures and the recent withdrawal of support from the United States Agency for International Development (USAID); said that to address the shortfall caused by USAID's pullout the ministry, in collaboration with the Ministry of Finance, were exploring innovative measures, including public-private partnerships, to close the funding gap; added that the ministry had also set up a Resource Mobilisation Unit and an Intersectoral Collaboration Unit to enhance efficiency and ensure that available resources were used for optimal impact.

a3430.speaker: Kwaku Saffu-Mensah, Principal Planner, Ministry of Health
a3430.speech: Said the government was focused on prioritising high-burden areas to reduce wastage and maximise impact; said the establishment of the National Vaccine Institute, passed by an Act of Parliament, was a major milestone in the push for local vaccine production and research.

a3430.speaker: Kwaku Saffu-Mensah, Principal Planner, Ministry of Health
a3430.speech: Said citizen involvement was crucial at every stage, saying, "Citizen participation builds legitimacy, trust, and accountability. It ensures that policies and funding decisions reflect the real needs of the people." ; said from pre-budget consultations to health sector hearings and even the parliamentary approval stage, there were multiple avenues for citizens, CSOs, and community leaders to contribute input and hold policymakers accountable.

a3525.speaker: Dr Philip Mpango, Vice President of Tanzania
a3525.speech: Said the tax-to-GDP ratio remains low, rising from 12.0 percent in 2001/02 to 14.9 percent in 2024/25, despite good progress in tax collection, and called for more systemic and policy-driven action ; emphasized that a stable and transparent tax regime is a key driver of economic growth and public welfare ; urged participants, including stakeholders from both public and private sectors, to develop strategic approaches for increasing domestic revenue, enabling the government to deliver better services to citizens and reduce reliance on foreign aid ; directed ministers across various sectors to actively contribute ideas through open discussions and digital platforms aimed at expanding national revenue streams.

a3525.speaker: Dr Philip Mpango, Vice President of Tanzania
a3525.speech: Reiterated the Sixth Phase Government’s commitment to enhancing Tanzania’s business and investment environment by strengthening security, maintaining peace, and ensuring a fair and equitable tax system ; outlined several government initiatives on tax reform, including the increased use of ICT in tax collection, the development of a comprehensive taxpayer database, and the reduction of non-productive tax exemptions.

a3525.speaker: Saada Mkuya, Minister of State for Finance and Planning (Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar)
a3525.speech: Reported that the government has already scrapped over 380 nuisance charges and continues to expand the use of digital platforms to simplify tax payment processes.

a3525.speaker: Angelina Ngalula, Chairperson of the Tanzania Private Sector Foundation (TPSF)
a3525.speech: Stressed the importance of tax education among both small and large-scale business owners to help broaden the taxpayer base; noted that Tanzania’s approximately two million registered taxpayers is still low relative to the country’s economic potential.

a3600.speaker: Abdikadir Kamil Mohamed, Prime Minister of Djibouti
a3600.speech: welcomed President Irro and his delegation at Djibouti's international airport and stated on behalf of President Ismail Omar Guelleh that the visit reflected a spirit of “trust and friendship.”

a3600.speaker: Abdirahman Mohamed Abdillahi Irro, President of Somaliland
a3600.speech: has recently stated that a major trade agreement with Ethiopia will likely be signed before the end of the year.

a3663.speaker: Food and Drugs Authority (FDA), Upper East Regional Office, Ghana
a3663.speech: Says a type of Postinor 2 with a pink flower label on the pack is not registered, and that the Authority could therefore not ascertain the safety and efficacy of the said brand, as it had not gone through the Authority's system.

a3663.speaker: Abel Ndego, Principal Regulatory Officer, Food and Drugs Authority (Upper East Region)
a3663.speech: "Postinor 2 is a drug we are all familiar with, and we know it is something we use for preventing pregnancies but this particular one with the pink flower, has not been registered by the FDA." ; "We have also undertaken quality product monitoring of this particular product, and we have noticed that the Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient that should instigate the ability of the product to prevent pregnancy is not at the required value. And so once you use it, you would not get the needed pharmaceutical implication."

a3663.speaker: Abel Ndego, Principal Regulatory Officer, Food and Drugs Authority (Upper East Region)
a3663.speech: Admonished members of the public to buy pharmaceutical products from accredited licensed pharmacies and over-the-counter sale outlets, saying "This way, you are sure that you are buying registered products and the products are stored under the requisite storage conditions." ; said the efficacy of medicines was directly linked to storage: "Storage affects medicine efficacy very seriously. We have medicines that are supposed to be in cool chain. They should be refrigerated." ; observed that some members of the public stored syrup medications for children on kitchen shelves instead of refrigerators, noting that the temperature in the kitchen could affect the efficacy of the medicine.

a3663.speaker: Abel Ndego, Principal Regulatory Officer, Food and Drugs Authority (Upper East Region)
a3663.speech: Said there were lots of products on the market claiming to cure all manner of diseases, and, showing one such unregistered product with images of a male sexual organ on it: "Even the packaging alone will tell you that this has not been approved by the FDA, because we would not allow this kind of obscene pictures on a product. But these are products that you would be surprised at the caliber of people who are purchasing them in the name of strengthening and elongating their organs. These have very dire health consequences on us."

a3782.speaker: The Wall Street Journal (analysis)
a3782.speech: Has analyzed the huge spending of the United States on aid to foreign countries, and found that the support of African countries has become one of the less successful ones.

a3841.speaker: International Monetary Fund (latest forecasts)
a3841.speech: According to the latest forecasts of the International Monetary Fund, the German economy is expected to stagnate, with no growth foreseen by the end of the year, after a 0.3% contraction last year; forecasts for 2025 are just as modest, with annual growth of only 0.8%.

a3841.speaker: Volkswagen
a3841.speech: Announced the closure of three plants, which will entail around 20,000 layoffs, a 10% reduction in wage costs and a freeze on pay increases for the next two years.

a3841.speaker: Olaf Scholz, German Chancellor
a3841.speech: Pointed the finger at the aid Germany has given Ukraine, asserting that this complex crisis results directly from Berlin's obligation to support Volodymyr Zelensky.

a3841.speaker: Dimap/ARD surveys
a3841.speech: According to the Dimap/ARD surveys, at the federal level the government's popularity has fallen below 20%, reaching barely 12% in Saxony.

a3841.speaker: Christian Lindner, former German Finance Minister
a3841.speech: Had openly warned that Germany could not sustain its economy while financing a war.

a3841.speaker: Annalena Baerbock, German Foreign Minister
a3841.speech: Underlined the financial weight of continued support for Ukraine, revealing that the 37 billion euros allocated required cuts in social programmes in Germany.

a3841.speaker: Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission
a3841.speech: In an anticipatory move of submission to the recently re-elected President Trump, aimed at avoiding American taxes on European products, proposed buying even more American LNG, making European and German industry even less competitive.

a3841.speaker: Federal Statistical Office (Destatis)
a3841.speech: According to the Federal Statistical Office (Destatis), the average age in Germany is 44.6 years.

a3890.speaker: Lovemore Makurirofa, Information, Research and Evaluation Officer at the Cancer Association of Zimbabwe (CAZ)
a3890.speech: Confirmed that programming has long been biased toward treatment rather than prevention. "People are taught to seek care only when signs and symptoms appear-high fever and weak joints for malaria, rice watery diarrhoea for cholera. That is how we have conditioned the population: wait for a sign, then go to the clinic," he said. ; Such mindset, he noted, is reinforced from childhood and as such, there is need to reframe public health messaging around NCDs. "Even when encouraged to get screened for NCDs like cancer, hypertension or diabetes, many respond, 'I'm fine-I feel healthy,' because they have been taught to seek care only when symptoms appear," he said.

a3890.speaker: Ministry of Health and Child Care (MOHCC) official (anonymous)
a3890.speech: Concurred, noting that while symptom-based messaging has assisted communities recognize illness early, it has left gaps in prevention, lifestyle education, and awareness of environmental factors like sanitation and hygiene. "The National Health Strategy (2021-2025) and National Development Strategy 1 (NDS1) provide a strong framework to address these gaps by ensuring that media campaigns balance symptom awareness with prevention-focused education. This will empower communities not only to know when to seek treatment but also how to protect and maintain their health," he said.

a3890.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a3890.speech: Underscores the importance of effective media communication, outlining six key standards, namely accessible, actionable, credible, relevant, timely, and understandable, for promoting healthier behaviours and driving policy change. ; The WHO recommends co-creating health content with community leaders, segmenting audiences by language and literacy, and integrating traditional and digital channels. It also urges specialized training for journalists, rapid feedback loops, robust monitoring and above all, it emphasizes equity, translating materials into all national languages, including sign language.

a3890.speaker: Itai Rusike, Executive Director of the Community Working Group on Health (CWGH)
a3890.speech: Added that while campaigns mention prevention, communities often engage "only when illness strikes and seek immediate relief before returning to risky behaviours like smoking, poor hygiene, and unsafe water use." ; Noted that screening is often seen as costly and inconvenient, especially when follow-up systems are weak yet, he argued, prevention saves money and lives.

a3890.speaker: 2022 policy brief co-authored by the Community Working Group on Health (CWGH)
a3890.speech: Calls for a "health for all, all for health" transformation, one that restores community decision-making and redesigns environments to support prevention.

a3890.speaker: Ministry of Health and Child Care (MOHCC) official (anonymous)
a3890.speech: Emphasized that preventive messages must use simple, clear language and local examples. "Practical steps like handwashing routines, balanced diets, or regular check-ups help turn information into habits that reduce disease risk," he said, adding however, poverty, limited access to health services, cultural beliefs, and stigma often hinder adoption. ; Agreed that prevention saves money, noting that preventive measures reduce hospital admissions and medical expenses, easing pressure on an overstretched system.

a3890.speaker: Lovemore Makurirofa, Cancer Association of Zimbabwe (CAZ)
a3890.speech: Noted that early-stage NCDs often do not show symptoms, making proactive education essential and he advocated for increased resources toward outreach teams that can engage communities directly, encouraging clinic visits even in the absence of illness. ; Stressed that changing public perception around non-communicable diseases requires more than just new messaging, it demands resources to undo years of conditioning. "This idea was taught and re-taught. When I present on cervical cancer and urge women to get screened, the first question is always, 'What signs should I look for?' They believe if they feel fine, screening isn't necessary." ; Said the mindset affects both women and men, noting that tests for blood pressure at workplaces would find people who need urgent care, but they would not go to hospital because they feel 'fit.' "They were taught to seek help only when something seems abnormal. That's the message we must correct," he said.

a3890.speaker: Ministry of Health and Child Care (MOHCC) official (anonymous)
a3890.speech: Added that regular check-ups help identify risks early, making treatment simpler and less costly, adding early detection prevents catastrophic health expenditure at individual and family level. He advocated for a "settings approach" to health promotion, delivering information and services through schools, workplaces, and community outreaches.

a3890.speaker: Lovemore Makurirofa, Cancer Association of Zimbabwe (CAZ)
a3890.speech: On screening access: "We need designated screening centres, just like we have for HIV testing. That way, anyone who wants to be screened knows where to go," said Makurirofa. ; "I think we'll get there soon, but right now, cervical cancer is killing many women," Makurirofa said.

a3890.speaker: Itai Rusike, Executive Director of the Community Working Group on Health (CWGH)
a3890.speech: Noted that the health sector in Zimbabwe operates within a narrow legal remit where key social determinants namely water, sanitation and nutrition, fall under other agencies, and when these systems fail, the Health Ministry is left managing the fallout. He also critiqued the health training, which he said follows a Western biomedical model, and often sidelining holistic, community-based methods rooted in Traditional African Medicine. ; With major funders like the Global Fund and USAID transitioning out by 2030, Rusike called for urgent reform to meet population growth and shifting disease patterns.

a3890.speaker: Ministry of Health and Child Care (MOHCC) official (anonymous)
a3890.speech: Said campaigns should promote healthy living, not just illness response, with nutrition, physical activity, vaccination, hygiene, and early detection being central. ; The media can help normalize health monitoring, said the MOHCC official, adding that sharing relatable success stories, highlighting role models, and using interactive formats like radio call-ins or social media Questions & Answers can shift public perception. "Over time, consistent messaging helps communities see health monitoring as a normal positive habit rather than something only done when illness occurs," he said.

a4096.speaker: Dr Kenneth Kaunda, first President of Zambia
a4096.speech: In May 1987 announced that Zambia was terminating her contract with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

a4096.speaker: Dr Kenneth Kaunda, first President of Zambia
a4096.speech: Was always encouraging Zambians that there was “light at the end of the tunnel.”

a4096.speaker: Dr Kenneth Kaunda, first President of Zambia
a4096.speech: By 1996 announced that he still wanted to go back to State House, as Republican president.

a4096.speaker: Dr Dambisa Moyo, author of the book Dead Aid
a4096.speech: In her book she counsels Third World countries to reduce their dependence on donor aid or altogether abandon foreign aid.

a4437.speaker: Moses Kunkuyu, Malawi Government spokesperson
a4437.speech: Has acknowledged the situation, stating that the government is implementing responsive measures.

a4883.speaker: Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs of France (signed op-ed)
a4883.speech: Wrote that it is the most vulnerable countries, those already bearing the full brunt of the consequences of the war in Ukraine, that will pay the heaviest price following the abrupt halt of the Black Sea grain accords, and that "this halt is irresponsible, while 2022 was a terrible year for food security"; recalled that the initiative had notably allowed the World Food Programme to feed thousands of people in need in Djibouti, Kenya, Ethiopia, Somalia, Sudan and Yemen.

a4883.speaker: Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs of France (signed op-ed)
a4883.speech: Wrote that the end of the Black Sea Initiative will translate into a significant reduction in the volumes of grain reaching the populations that need it most - the accords had allowed 33 million tonnes of food products to pass to 45 countries in one year - and that the donations announced by Russia, with no precise date and limited to a handful of countries and a few thousand tonnes, "represent a tiny fraction of the humanitarian aid that was provided via the Black Sea by the World Food Programme. This minimal and cosmetic gesture, displayed on the occasion of a Summit, fools no one."

a4883.speaker: Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs of France (signed op-ed)
a4883.speech: Wrote that the abrupt halt of the accords by Russia will also make grain prices even more volatile, that prices reached their sharpest increase on 19 July and risk rising further in the medium term, and asked: "Who profits from this increase? Russia and its agricultural sector, which wants to enrich itself at the expense of the most destitute and whose exports are, whatever it may say, subject to no sanctions. Russia is indeed hoping to reach a record. It is accumulating stocks and harvests in order to sell more and at a higher price. The rest of the world will suffer from its decisions."

a4883.speaker: Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs of France (signed op-ed)
a4883.speech: Wrote that Ukraine, a country at war, part of whose territory is illegally occupied and whose population is daily the victim of bombardments, is managing to mobilise in favour of global food security, having launched the humanitarian initiative "Grain From Ukraine" for the benefit of the most vulnerable countries in Africa and Asia.

a4883.speaker: Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs of France (signed op-ed)
a4883.speech: Wrote that, conversely, Russia is deliberately striking the ports of Odesa, Mykolaiv and Chornomorsk, destroying grain silos and firing on civilian ships, and that in doing so it is openly violating international law, driving up grain prices on the markets after each of its attacks, and destroying and preventing the passage of reserves that were going to the World Food Programme and hence to the populations that suffer the most - "With what objectives if not to make food a weapon?" ; "Making hunger a weapon of political coercion, that is the point to which Russia has sunk. Once again, as it has constantly done for a year and a half, it is violating an elementary principle of our common morality."

a4883.speaker: Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs of France (signed op-ed)
a4883.speech: Wrote that, faced with this cynical use of the food weapon by Russia, "France and its European partners have chosen the path of responsibility and international solidarity": France mobilised at national level more than 840 million euros in food aid over the past year, including nearly 250 million euros of emergency aid; it contributes to the European Union's "solidarity corridors," which have allowed more than 38 million tonnes of grain to be exported from Ukraine by road, rail and river; and while Russia has reduced its contribution to the World Food Programme, France has given the WFP reinforced financial and material support to deliver grain and fertiliser to the countries that need them most ; France will continue its efforts, notably in October in Paris at the summit of the coalition for school meals and at the forthcoming summit on nutrition that France will host, and recalled the summit for a new global financing pact held in Paris on 22 and 23 June ; "Faced with this, France will act tirelessly, with its partners, so that those who need it most can feed themselves as they should. We, for our part, will remain faithful to our principles."

a4883.speaker: United Nations (cited figures)
a4883.speech: According to the United Nations, 735 million people suffer from hunger in the world, one person in five on the African continent.

a4980.speaker: Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (statement)
a4980.speech: According to a statement from the ministry, Abdelatty reaffirmed to Boulos Egypt's principled stance on Sudan and set out Cairo's diplomatic efforts.

a4980.speaker: Badr Abdelatty, Egyptian Foreign Minister
a4980.speech: reaffirmed to Masad Boulos Egypt's principled stance that "Sudan's unity and sovereignty are non-negotiable"; rejected any attempt to partition the country and emphasised the need for a Sudanese-led political process as the only credible path toward lasting peace ; urged full implementation of the International Quartet's September 12 declaration, which calls for an immediate humanitarian truce and a comprehensive ceasefire.

a4980.speaker: Masad Boulos, US President's adviser for Arab and Middle Eastern affairs
a4980.speech: outlined ongoing efforts by the United States and the Quartet - comprising Washington, London, Riyadh and Abu Dhabi - to end violations in conflict zones, particularly in Darfur.

a4980.speaker: Badr Abdelatty, Egyptian Foreign Minister
a4980.speech: stressed in his conversation with Fletcher the need to intensify international coordination to ensure humanitarian aid reaches the most affected regions ; highlighted his country's concrete contributions, including regular relief shipments through the Egypt-Sudan border, the reception of refugees, and continued cooperation with the African Union, the UN and other international organisations to keep humanitarian channels open.

a4980.speaker: Tom Fletcher, UN Assistant Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs
a4980.speech: said he would raise before the UN Security Council the "flagrant violations" committed against civilians, while commending Cairo's active role in facilitating cross-border humanitarian assistance.

a5075.speaker: Zimbabwe Mercantile Exchange (ZMX)
a5075.speech: Says it is set to benefit from the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA)'s standardisation and mutual recognition of commodity grades, and prices.

a5188.speaker: Communities in Traditional Authorities Chamba and Ntonda, Mangochi district
a5188.speech: Have commended the Titukulane Resilience Food Security Activity for constructing new and rehabilitating existing, but dysfunctional boreholes in the two areas.

a5188.speaker: Village Head Chiyambeni, Traditional Authority Ntonda, Mangochi
a5188.speech: Said the problem of lack of safe and clean drinking water negatively affected the social and economic development of his area ; stated that the high levels of destitution and poverty in the area are a result of lack of water, observing that without safe and clean drinking water, the possibility of breaking out of the cycle of poverty is incredibly slim ; “Lack of water and poverty are inseparably linked because where there is no water, able-bodied members of a community are forced to spend hours searching and transporting water instead of working on their farms. Additionally, poor access to water and insufficient sanitation affect the health of the poor, their food security, and their prospects for making a living” ; emphasized that the construction and rehabilitation of the boreholes have reduced cases of waterborne diseases in the targeted areas ; “We will now actively participate in the social and economic activities taking place in our communities.”

a5188.speaker: Theresa Kananji, 50, widow from Chiyambeni Village who lost her husband to cholera
a5188.speech: Said her spouse would not have died if the village had access to safe and clean drinking water ; described the construction of the borehole as a great relief and salvation not only to her family, but also to the entire village ; “I am very excited with the coming in of a borehole in our village. We used to walk long distances to fetch water from unsafe sources. It would take three hours for someone to walk to and from the water source” ; “This borehole will significantly reduce cases of cases of cholera and other waterborne diseases thereby saving lives. We're very grateful to Care International in Malawi and its partners for giving us this precious gift.”

a5188.speaker: Solomon Chirwa, WaterAid Malawi Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) specialist
a5188.speech: Said the project has helped significantly in improving knowledge, attitudes, skills and norms related to essential sanitation and hygiene behaviors ; stated that there is now increased availability of basic safely managed facilities and consumables necessary for essential sanitation and hygiene practices ; “Through the same project, we also provided technical assistance in WASH policy review, WASH planning including integrated planning and performance review with other sectors especially at policy and district levels. We also advocated for increased funding for the WASH sector that recognizes and promotes complementarity with other sectors such as health, education and gender.”

a5447.speaker: Progress report, second edition (International Organization for Migration and Georgetown University)
a5447.speech: According to the recently published conclusions of the second edition of the Progress report, more than 58.5 million people have been forced to flee their homes while remaining in their country of origin, an alarming increase explained by a combination of armed conflict, intercommunal violence and natural disasters linked to climate change; sixty per cent of these people would prefer to stay where they are rather than return to their community of origin ; the trend is even more marked among people displaced by disasters for more than five years, 96% of whom wish to stay where they are, calling into question the received idea that return to the region of origin is always preferable ; security appears as the determining factor in the choice to stay for 71% of people, while economic opportunities also play a crucial role, particularly for long-duration displacement; the analysis draws on data from 15 distinct countries ; according to the report, as the number of internally displaced people continues to rise, it is imperative to rethink traditional approaches and focus on durable solutions that take account of the preferences and real needs of displaced people.

a5447.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a5447.speech: In 2015, the IOM was already reporting more than 1.4 million displaced people in six north-eastern Nigerian states, with a majority of women and children among the displaced.

a5722.speaker: Delta Shila, AMDT Monitoring and Results Measurement Officer
a5722.speech: Speaking in Babati, Manyara, reported that between June and September this year, the project directly reached 600 farmers growing mung bean, cowpea and pigeon pea. ; "The VACS project focuses on improving agricultural productivity and nutrition by promoting diverse, climate-resilient crops and healthy soil management. The goal is to build awareness through demo plots, field days, and strengthen farmer-to-off-taker links."

a5722.speaker: Delta Shila, AMDT Monitoring and Results Measurement Officer
a5722.speech: Encouraged farmers to adopt high-quality seeds and embrace drip irrigation to counter climate challenges and increase yield.

a5722.speaker: Dodoo Matambo, 60-year-old lead farmer from Gedemar village and project beneficiary
a5722.speech: Shared his success story, saying after receiving training on drip irrigation, he can now farm three to four times a year, without relying on rain-fed agriculture.

a5722.speaker: Zabron Mbwaga, Managing Director of BEULA Seed Company
a5722.speech: Confirmed their commitment to supporting under-utilised crops, noting that they aim to reach 800 farmers by December 2024 through the VACS project.

a5789.speaker: Gola Boyoi, Chief Administrator of Greater Pibor Administrative Area
a5789.speech: Blamed his Eastern Equatoria counterpart for closing off the important route that serves as a lifeline road to Jebal Boma and Vertet counties in Pibor; stated that the road closure has posed a significant challenge and left communities without access to food commodities, that the route was closed since April this year due to insecurities caused by a communal conflict, and that the situation has worsened other challenges facing Jebel Boma residents as the road to Juba and the local airstrip remain dysfunctional due to rainy season. “The Eastern Equatoria State government closed off the Kapoita to Buma Road since April due to the communal conflict affecting the transportation of the goods and accessibility for residents of Jebel Boma and Vertet Maruwo counties, who mainly depend on the highway for their basic necessities,” he said. ; “The Boma road connectivity within the counties of the GPAA hinders humanitarian assistance, effort and security operations and agricultural activities and access to the market.” ; “The Buma air strip operates exclusively during the dry season and is rendered non-operational during the post rains and flooding season.”

a5789.speaker: Luis Lobong, Governor of Eastern Equatoria State
a5789.speech: Responding to the statement, pointed out that the road was closed after thousands of armed men from Pibor launched a deadly attack on the Kapoeta region; said the highway closed automatically and it was not the making of his government; threatened to take legal action against the accusation if the forum will not address and correct the report by his Pibor counterpart. “People may think it is only the government of Eastern Equatoria being accused. I don’t think if we write that the government, and one of its levels closed the road that is a lifeline to the people of South Sudan.” ; “I want to report that if this thing is not discussed and withdrawn, the government of Eastern Equatoria will have no other option but to take a legal action against the administrative government of Greater Pibor.” ; “If it is not corrected, we will take a legal action. Because such a report has been discussed, presented to the Council of Ministers, which means it has been approved by the whole government of Greater Pibor.”

a5910.speaker: Ethiopian Statistics Service (survey)
a5910.speech: According to a survey published by the Ethiopian Statistics Service, close to half of the 1.2 million smallholder farmers in Tigray use chemical fertilisers.

a5910.speaker: People close to the matter (anonymous)
a5910.speech: Said Phiri’s request was accepted by Minister Oumer on condition, with the Agriculture Ministry wanting to be involved in quality inspection and approval of laboratory results suppliers provide FAO before the fertiliser is allowed in.

a5910.speaker: Oumer Hussien, Minister of Agriculture of Ethiopia (letter to FAO representative Phiri)
a5910.speech: “This is to ensure the quality of fertiliser matches the country's standards,” reads a letter Minister Oumer dispatched to Phiri.

a5910.speaker: Oumer Hussien, Minister of Agriculture of Ethiopia
a5910.speech: Told Phiri he had approved his request due to the global shortage of fertilisers and the scarcity of foreign currency the country is experiencing.

a5910.speaker: Sileshi Getahun, advisor to Sofia Kassa (PhD), state minister for Agriculture
a5910.speech: “The newly-established Agricultural Authority will take over the supervision role next year.”

a5910.speaker: Gashaw Aycheluhim, communications director at the Ethiopian Agricultural Businesses Corporation
a5910.speech: The Corporation's executives say they are not aware of the deal with the FAO: “We haven’t received confirmation from the Ministry.”

a5910.speaker: Food & Agriculture Organisation (FAO) (statement)
a5910.speech: Says the procurement process for the first batch of fertiliser is already ongoing – “Some of the fertiliser is already in the country,” reads a statement FAO issued ; A statement sent to Fortune says FAO faces an 85 million dollar deficit to buy the remaining amount and is discussing with development partners to secure the funds.

a5910.speaker: Those close to the issue (anonymous)
a5910.speech: Fear that the procurement might be too late for farmers in the region.

a5910.speaker: Lemma Dagabassa, lecturer at Haromaya University’s school of plant sciences
a5910.speech: Foresees the procurement of fertilisers will mean little for farmers in Tigray as the time for planting has already passed ; “Due to years of soil erosion, the region is among the areas that require chemical fertilisers to compensate for the loss of nutrients in the soil.”

a5967.speaker: Gates Foundation (press announcement)
a5967.speech: A new partnership announced today between the Gates Foundation and Indian manufacturer Hetero Labs (Hetero) - supported by upfront funding and volume guarantees - will enable the company to manufacture generic lenacapavir at roughly $40 per patient per year (after a short pre-treatment oral regimen), a price point designed to make the breakthrough treatment affordable for national health systems.

a5967.speaker: Dr. Vamsi Krishna, managing director of Hetero Group of Companies
a5967.speech: "Hetero is pleased to partner with the Gates Foundation to create a pathway for the sustainable and affordable supply of lenacapavir. This collaboration reflects our commitment to ensuring access to innovative HIV medicines for patients in India and other low- and middle-income countries."

a5967.speaker: Unitaid, the Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI), and Wits RHI
a5967.speech: Announced new commitments with Dr. Reddy's Laboratories Ltd. (DRL), another Indian manufacturer, reinforcing efforts to build a competitive generics ecosystem.

a5967.speaker: Public health experts
a5967.speech: See it as a transformative option for people who face barriers to daily oral PrEP, including stigma, adherence challenges, and inconsistent access to medication.

a5967.speaker: Modeling study on lenacapavir scale-up
a5967.speech: Modeling suggests that the introduction of lenacapavir has the potential to prevent significant numbers of HIV infections. In fact, one study showed that scaling up access to affordable lenacapavir to just 4% of the population in high-burden countries could prevent up to 20% of new infections.

a5967.speaker: Trevor Mundel, president of global health at the Gates Foundation
a5967.speech: "Scientific advances like lenacapavir can help us end the HIV epidemic-if they are made accessible to people who can benefit from them the most. We are committed to ensuring that those at highest risk, who can least afford it, aren't left behind."

a5967.speaker: Bill Gates, Chair of the Gates Foundation
a5967.speech: Earlier this week, Chair Bill Gates announced the foundation's $912 million pledge to the Global Fund's 2026-2028 replenishment fundraising campaign, which aims to save 23 million lives from HIV, malaria, and tuberculosis between 2027 and 2029.

a5967.speaker: Bill Gates, Chair of the Gates Foundation
a5967.speech: Earlier this year, Gates made a historic announcement that he would give away virtually all of his wealth to the foundation to accelerate progress on saving and improving lives. He also announced the foundation would spend $200 billion over the next 20 years, working with its partners to make as much progress as possible toward three primary goals: end preventable deaths of moms and babies; ensure the next generation grows up without having to suffer from deadly infectious diseases; and lift millions of people out of poverty, putting them on a path to prosperity. At the end of the 20-year period, the foundation will sunset its operations.

a5967.speaker: Kate Hampton, CEO of the Children's Investment Fund Foundation
a5967.speech: "The deals announced today on generics are a major step forward in ending the HIV epidemic. They build on full value-chain investments by CIFF and others to foster a competitive market so that access to lenacapavir is affordable and reliable for all those who need it."

a6094.speaker: The Lancet study (research published in The Lancet medical journal)
a6094.speech: Deep funding cuts to the U.S. Agency for International Development and its potential dismantling could result in more than 14 million additional deaths by 2030 ; The study estimated that over the past two decades, USAID-funded programs have prevented more than 91 million deaths globally, including 30 million deaths among children. Projections suggest that ongoing deep funding cuts - combined with the potential dismantling of the agency - could result in more than 14 million additional deaths by 2030, including 4.5 million deaths among children younger than 5 years ; "Our estimates show that, unless the abrupt funding cuts announced and implemented in the first half of 2025 are reversed, a staggering number of avoidable deaths could occur by 2030." ; USAID funding has had a crucial role in improving global health, primarily directed toward low and middle-income countries, particularly African nations, according to the study.

a6094.speaker: U.S. government
a6094.speech: says the funding cuts to USAID and its aid programs worldwide are part of its broader plan to remove wasteful spending.

a6094.speaker: Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State
a6094.speech: said in March the Trump administration canceled over 80% of all programs at USAID following a six-week review. The remaining approximately 1,000 programs, he said, would now be administered "more effectively" under the U.S. State Department and in consultation with Congress.

a6275.speaker: Ambassador John N. Nkengasong, Global AIDS Coordinator and senior official of the Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy of the US State Department
a6275.speech: At the virtual press conference of 10 October organized by the Media Center for the US State Department, shared with the audience the President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief in Africa (PEPFAR), the importance of establishing solid public-private partnerships for the sustainability of the response, and of government ownership and leadership in the HIV/AIDS response; explained how the US government intends to approach its journey up to 2030 and beyond 2030 by supporting the HIV/AIDS response, and reviewed the road travelled over the last 21 years.

a6275.speaker: Ambassador John N. Nkengasong, Global AIDS Coordinator (US State Department)
a6275.speech: “Botswana has achieved this objective (inaudible)” — said Botswana has reached the three 95 targets set by UNAIDS ; said the fight against HIV/AIDS is not over, “so we must maintain this response, continue to treat infected people and prevent rates of new infections.”

a6275.speaker: Ambassador John N. Nkengasong, Global AIDS Coordinator (US State Department)
a6275.speech: “It is a retrovirus, which means that it will take considerable efforts, if we are lucky enough to have a vaccine and a cure, to be able to say that we have eradicated HIV or eliminated HIV, just as we did for polio, as we are doing for polio or smallpox” ; said that we must think about maintaining the gains made over the last 21 years, in order to keep people on treatment and ensure that the rate of newly infected people decreases.

a6275.speaker: Ambassador John N. Nkengasong, Global AIDS Coordinator (US State Department)
a6275.speech: Considered that the dialogue is as follows: how can we reach our 2030 targets, agreed within the framework of the Sustainable Development Goals, to end HIV/AIDS as a public health threat, and look beyond 2030? ; “the road to that goal begins with clear conversations with partner countries like Botswana to say, what can we do and what can you do so that we can continue? It is not about ending PEPFAR, it is rather about building the way forward on the basis of the success we have obtained so far.”

a6325.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a6325.speech: Has raised alarms, projecting that by 2026, the Federal Government could spend nearly 100 per cent of its revenue just on servicing its existing debts.

a6325.speaker: Bismarck Rewane, CEO of Financial Derivatives
a6325.speech: Has been vocal in highlighting the negative impact of this debt burden. He pointed out that debt servicing is so consuming that it has crippled the government's ability to invest in infrastructure and essential services. For instance, the N8 trillion spent on debt servicing in 2023 could have been used to build 5,000 kilometres of dual carriage roads, 1,600 schools, 80,000 healthcare centres, or generate 5,000 MW of solar power.

a6325.speaker: World Bank
a6325.speech: Has attempted to reassure global stakeholders by describing Nigeria's debt as “statistically sustainable.” However, it has also cautioned that the country's debt remains “vulnerable and costly.”

a6369.speaker: Union of News Agencies of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (UNA)
a6369.speech: A number of directors of international news agencies and experts from international organisations and humanitarian institutions will speak at the round table, UNA reports.

a6369.speaker: Mohammad bin Abd Rabbo Al-Yami, Director General of the Union of News Agencies of the OIC (UNA)
a6369.speech: explained that the round table will discuss strengthening the role of the media in supporting humanitarian work and highlighting the relief efforts of international actors in this field, led by the King Salman Centre for Relief and Humanitarian Aid. ; Al-Yami indicated that the round table will seek, through its deliberations, “to arrive at a clear vision of the relationship between the media in their various forms and humanitarian work, and to develop recommendations in this regard,” stressing that the round table will also discuss the challenges facing the media in the African Sahel and Lake Chad region in dealing professionally with humanitarian crises and contributing to mitigating them.

a6397.speaker: Mohamud Moalim, Director of Somalia's Disaster Management Agency (SODMA)
a6397.speech: Revealed on Saturday that the northeastern Puntland state had refused federal assistance in providing medical treatment to soldiers injured in the ongoing conflict against ISIS militants ; speaking from Jalalaqsi town in Hiran region, said that he personally reached out to Puntland President Saeed Abdullahi Deni, requesting permission for SODMA to evacuate the wounded soldiers for treatment and to deliver humanitarian aid to those in need.

a6397.speaker: Mohamud Moalim, Director of Somalia's Disaster Management Agency (SODMA)
a6397.speech: Expressed concern over the situation, highlighting the paradox of regional states, which were established to decentralize public services and ensure that every Somali citizen has access to vital services, now obstructing the delivery of humanitarian assistance. He likened the refusal to that of Al-Shabaab insurgents. He questioned the government's ability to distribute humanitarian aid effectively if parts of the country, including regions controlled by Al-Shabaab, remain inaccessible and regional authorities themselves act as barriers.

a6397.speaker: Saeed Abdullahi Deni, Puntland President
a6397.speech: Reportedly rejected the request, citing his ongoing political dispute with Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud and Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre, though no further explanation was provided.

a6397.speaker: Puntland officials
a6397.speech: Have yet to respond to Moalim's comments.

a6574.speaker: Sidi Tiémoko Touré, Minister of Animal and Fisheries Resources of Côte d'Ivoire
a6574.speech: Took the opportunity at the Fratenité Matin Exchange Forum to set out the difficulties facing the animal and fisheries resources sector, and said that to address them real investment opportunities are emerging for all Ivorians, stressing that animal and fisheries resources in Côte d'Ivoire are an under-exploited sector even though it constitutes "a real investment opportunity" ; said Côte d'Ivoire needs 650 thousand tonnes of fish every year but records barely 100 tonnes of local production, spending an average of 350 billion CFA francs on imports to fill the deficit ; confided that "Côte d'Ivoire is a country that imports so much fish. That is why we are creating the ecosystem with the establishment of aquaculture zones," before stating that "it is possible to make money in fish farming."

a6574.speaker: Sidi Tiémoko Touré, Minister of Animal and Fisheries Resources of Côte d'Ivoire
a6574.speech: Gave an overview of the animal and fisheries resources sector and presented the 2024 roadmap, centred on the government's National Policy for the Development of Livestock, Fisheries and Aquaculture (Ponadepa 2022-2026), whose financing is estimated at 1,049 billion CFA francs.

a6599.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of the Republic of Ghana (signed instrument of removal, Presidential Seal affixed)
a6599.speech: “Now therefore, know ye all men that I, John Dramani Mahama, President of the Republic of Ghana, in pursuance of the said Article 146 (9), do hereby REMOVE the said Chief Justice, Gertrude Araba Esaaba Sackey Torkornoo, from the office of Chief Justice and Justice of the Supreme Court, with effect from the date hereof. In witness whereof, I have hereunto set my hand caused the Presidential Seal to be affixed at Accra this 1st of Sept 2025.”

a6599.speaker: Presidency of Ghana (press statement, September 1, 2025)
a6599.speech: Explained that the removal was in accordance with Article 149 (9) of the 1992 Constitution ; “President John Dramani Mahama has, in accordance with Article 146(9) of the 1992 Constitution, removed the Chief Justice, Her Ladyship Justice Gertrude Araba Esaaba Sackey Torkonoo, from office with immediate effect. This follows receipt of the report of the Committee constituted under Article 146(6) to inquire into a petition submitted by a Ghanaian citizen, Mr Daniel Ofori. After considering the petition and the evidence, the Committee found that the grounds of stated misbehaviour under Article 146(1) had been established and recommended her removal from office. Under Article 146(9), the President is required to act in accordance with the committee's recommendation.”

a6599.speaker: Committee of inquiry chaired by Justice Gabriel Scott Pwamang, Justice of the Supreme Court (report)
a6599.speech: Within a four-month period of hearing, found that the grounds of stated misbehaviour under Article 146(1) had been established and recommended her removal from office.

a6599.speaker: 1992 Constitution of Ghana, Article 146 (9)
a6599.speech: Specifically stipulates that “The President shall, in each case, act in accordance with the recommendations of the committee”.

a6599.speaker: Daniel Ofori, Ghanaian citizen (petition)
a6599.speech: Petitioned the President to remove Justice Torkornoo on grounds of stated misbehaviour as Chief Justice.

a6628.speaker: United Kingdom (government position)
a6628.speech: Formally recognized Morocco’s Autonomy Proposal for the Sahara—originally submitted in 2007—as the most credible, viable, and pragmatic basis for a lasting resolution to the long-standing regional dispute, and emphasized its intention to act bilaterally, economically, regionally, and internationally in alignment with this stance.

a6628.speaker: Joint Communiqué signed by UK Foreign Secretary David Lammy and Morocco’s Foreign Minister Nasser Bourita
a6628.speech: The statement highlights that settling the Sahara issue is key to strengthening not only North Africa’s stability but also fostering economic cooperation and integration across the region and beyond ; acknowledges the strong leadership of His Majesty King Mohammed VI and notes the positive momentum surrounding the Sahara issue under his vision ; states the UK’s readiness to support development projects in the region through the UK Export Finance’s £5 billion commitment.

a6628.speaker: United Kingdom and Morocco (joint statement)
a6628.speech: Both countries reaffirmed their support for the UN-led process and the efforts of the Secretary General’s Personal Envoy, Mr. Staffan de Mistura.

a6628.speaker: United Kingdom (as permanent member of the UN Security Council)
a6628.speech: Expressed its readiness to actively engage with the parties involved to find a durable solution.

a6686.speaker: SADC (own descriptions, records and updates)
a6686.speech: SADC's own descriptions of the Troika's structure and mandate confirm how this rotating trio steers policy and security coordination across the region ; SADC records describe how this Troika machinery operates and why the incoming chair's voice matters throughout the cycle ; SADC updates around the 2018 handover describe how an incoming chair receives briefings on integration files and summit hosting standards, which show the practical work a deputy chair can start immediately.

a6686.speaker: Local and regional notices
a6686.speech: Recorded the decision and noted that the deputy chair supports the chair in guiding peace and security cooperation during the term.

a6743.speaker: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) report
a6743.speech: points to “an imminent and substantial likelihood of famine, owing to the rapid deterioration of the situation in the Gaza Strip” ; “The famine thresholds may already have been crossed, or will be crossed in the near future,” according to this report ; the situation has deteriorated in the north of the Gaza Strip with the collapse of food systems, a fall in humanitarian aid and a critical situation in terms of water, sanitation and hygiene, the report stresses ; “We can therefore estimate that hunger, malnutrition and excess mortality due to malnutrition and disease are increasing rapidly,” the document reads.

a6743.speaker: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) report
a6743.speech: According to the report, the number of aid shipments allowed into the Gaza Strip is now at its lowest level since October 2023 ; prices are soaring on the black market: gas has risen 2,612%, petrol 1,315% and wood 250%, according to the report ; “Alongside the extremely high prices of essential goods, which continue to rise, the livelihoods that allow us to buy or barter for food and other basic necessities have collapsed,” states the UN document.

a6743.speaker: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) report of 17 October, produced by NGOs and UN agencies including the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)
a6743.speech: estimated that some 345,000 inhabitants of Gaza would face hunger at a “catastrophic” level between November and April 2025, that is 16% of the population.

a6743.speaker: Israeli forces
a6743.speech: launched a large-scale, high-intensity operation in the north of the Gaza Strip in October, stating that they wanted to prevent the Islamist movement Hamas, responsible for the attack of 7 October 2023, from reconstituting its combat units.

a6743.speaker: Authorities of the Gaza enclave, controlled by Hamas
a6743.speech: The Israeli military offensive has already caused more than 43,000 deaths in the Gaza Strip, according to the authorities of the enclave.

a6763.speaker: Philippe Lazzarini, Commissioner-General of the UN agency for Palestinian refugees (UNRWA)
a6763.speech: Said a severe famine in the Gaza Strip can be averted if aid is allowed in: "The last time UNRWA was able to deliver food aid to northern Gaza was on 23 January" ; "Since then, together with other UN agencies, we have warned against a looming famine, appealed for regular humanitarian access, and stated that famine can be averted if more food convoys are allowed into northern Gaza on a regular basis" ; "Our calls to send food aid have been denied and have fallen on deaf ears." ; "This is a man-made disaster. The world committed to never let famine happen again. Famine can still be avoided through genuine political will to grant access and protection to meaningful assistance" ; "the days to come will once again test our common humanity and values."

a6763.speaker: United Nations
a6763.speech: According to the UN, the Israeli war on Gaza has pushed 85% of the territory's population into internal displacement amid acute shortages of food, clean water and medicine, while 60% of the enclave's infrastructure has been damaged or destroyed.

a6763.speaker: International Court of Justice (interim ruling)
a6763.speech: An interim ruling in January ordered Tel Aviv to stop genocidal acts and take measures to guarantee that humanitarian assistance is provided to civilians in Gaza.

a6791.speaker: International Society for Civil Liberties and Rule of Law (Intersociety) (special report)
a6791.speech: Noted that Nigeria “is headquartering no fewer than 22 terrorist cells with links or potential links to the Islamic State”; named Benue, Plateau states and Southern Kaduna communities as the top hotbeds of terrorists and jihadist killings in Nigeria in 2025, with Benue worst hit including the Yelewata massacre of June 13 to 14 that led to death of 280 persons and the Sankera massacre of April 2025 ; “Plateau State came second with estimated 806 deaths including more than 300 massacred in April 2025 alone; followed by Southern Kaduna with estimated 620 deaths including dozens abducted and killed in captivity and over 40 confirmed killed in Kauru part of Southern Kaduna as well as hundreds of others killed in the past 220 days of 2025.” ; “Christian leaders in Southern Kaduna State are also facing government embargo or censorship since late 2024, during which the victims of armed Fulani herdsmen attacks were banned from reporting to the media, human rights groups and others against unchecked and untracked killings and abductions perpetrated by bandits.” ; “The state also recorded the second largest number of abductions after Niger State, with estimated 800 including the December 2, 2024 abduction of 229 persons by the jihadists near Rijana Nigerian Army base in Kachia Local Government Area of the state.” ; “The Igbo land South-East came fourth with estimated 615 deaths fuelled by an upsurge in rural Igbo area jihadists' attacks and abductions and allied killings targeted at Southeasterners travelling within and outside the region.” Also identified Niger State as one of the worst hit states with estimated 605 deaths.

a6791.speaker: International Society for Civil Liberties and Rule of Law (Intersociety) (organisation)
a6791.speech: Called on the international community to designate Nigeria as “a country of particular concern and jihadist Fulani herdsmen as entities of particular concern” particularly by the government of the United States under President Donald Trump.

a6791.speaker: Emeka Umeagbalasi, Head of the Intersociety
a6791.speech: “These economies and democracies must also review hundreds of millions of dollars' worth of annual humanitarian, democracy, military and development assistance to Nigeria and have them tied as a condition for further assistance to the country and its leaders, insisting that they must rise to the occasion by respecting and protecting Fundamental Human Rights to Freedom of Thought, Conscience and Religion. Nigerian leaders must also internationally be compelled to decisively deal with the jihadist Fulani herdsmen including holding them accountable for massacring average of 6000 persons annually.”

a6791.speaker: Barrister Chidinma Udegbunam, Head of Publicity, and Barrister Ogoo Obi, Deputy Head of Int'l Justice and Human Rights (Intersociety)

a7037.speaker: Ifeoma Malo, founder and CEO of Clean Tech Hub
a7037.speech: Stated that Clean Tech Hub oversees the process of ensuring proper representation of women and Nigeria in global climate and environmental discourse and activities, and that the winners would receive equity-free grants of up to $200,000, access to a global investor network, and long-term entrepreneurship opportunities.

a7037.speaker: USAID
a7037.speech: Says the Climate Gender Equity Fund “will increase access to climate finance for gender-responsive, women-led, and women-benefiting organisations that address climate change.”

a7099.speaker: Scholars and analysts in Tanzania (experts in political and economic affairs)
a7099.speech: Advise African countries to organise themselves for self-reliance and to prepare for a difficult period of self-reliance, and to choose agendas that match these policy changes, while citing several issues, including migrants and the emphasis on abortion, as the things that brought down Trump's Democratic opponent, Kamala Harris.

a7099.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a7099.speech: Once called African countries, Haiti and El Salvador "shithole countries", complaining that many migrants come from those countries into his own ; When he came to power in 2016 he called Africans lazy and foolish, saying that all they know is eating, having sex and crime.

a7099.speaker: African Union
a7099.speech: Has already asked the United States Congress to extend AGOA by at least 10 years to continue the programme, a request that may hit a wall.

a7099.speaker: Ibrahim Rabby, analyst of international affairs
a7099.speech: Said Trump's victory has many interpretations for Africa, the big question being whether he will be the same as in his first term of 2016 to 2020 or whether he will be new: "Africa needs to understand that Trump's policies cannot change because right from his campaign process he did not show any sign of changing anything, especially when it comes to foreign affairs; he looks more at America and his slogan America Great Again" ; Said that if America cannot get anything from Africa it will not pursue any country, but will act on the basis of relations and benefit: "For example, in the Middle East he will continue with countries that give America benefit, including Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, and he will cut relations with countries that want to depend on that nation" ; "Trump is avoiding what America has been doing for many years for Africa. There is something to learn from the years 2016 to 2020: we witnessed African countries carrying out many coups because America, which was seen as the world's prefect, avoided its responsibilities and stopped looking at Africa" ; Said President Joe Biden has not visited Africa any more than Kamala Harris, and that with Trump's victory Africa must decide to be self-reliant ; "Trump's foreign policies are clear and you do not need to go to a classroom to learn what he is thinking; changes will occur especially in institutions. In his past term many institutions were closed for lack of funding."

a7099.speaker: Innocent Shoo, lecturer at the Salim Ahmed Salim College of Diplomacy
a7099.speech: Says African countries need to tighten their belts because Trump will curb illegal immigration and the giving of aid: "African leaders need to come up with an agenda to curb young people who sneak off to Europe and America in search of a better life. Trump is fed up; he has said that when he takes office he is going to expel all illegal immigrants" ; Said Trump's outlook is to heal America and restore that nation's capacity, and that Africa should organise itself because he has already rung the bell ; "We expect the wars in Gaza and Israel, and on the Middle East side, will perhaps end, including Sudan as well. He will try to end those wars by talking with the leaders of those countries, so it will help bring down the price of oil."

a7099.speaker: Dr Balozi Morwa, lecturer at Mbeya Catholic University College (CUCoM)
a7099.speech: Said Trump has been elected with the aim of ending the wars going on in various parts of the world: "Many American citizens have been complaining that their tax money is being used to run the war in Ukraine and Russia. With those wars ended, Africa will benefit from oil resources falling in price" ; Said those wars have pushed up the price of oil because they use that energy on a large scale, so with their end a great blessing will emerge and European nations will begin to look towards Africa.

a7157.speaker: Dr Mwigulu Nchemba, Minister for Finance of Tanzania
a7157.speech: Presented the national budget speech in Dodoma, where he announced that the government plans to collect and spend a total of 56.49tr/- in the 2025/26 financial year; stated that the budget is expected to be financed through domestic revenue amounting to 40.47 tr/-, grants amounting to 1.07 tr/- and loans totalling 14.95tr/-. “Out of the expected domestic revenue, tax revenue will amount to 32.31 tr/-, nontax revenue 6.48 tr/- and revenue from Local Government Authorities will be 1.68 tr/-. Furthermore, loans include 6.27tr/- from domestic sources and 8.68 trillion shillings from external sources,” he explained. ; Said the expenditure estimates include salaries and pension contributions (Central Government) amounting to 9.17tr/-, procurement of goods and services at 5.58tr/-, interest payments on loans totalling 6.49tr/-, subsidies to government institutions, public corporations and local government authorities amounting to 22.17 tr/- and 7.72 tr/- allocated for capital payments on domestic and foreign debt.

a7157.speaker: Dr Mwigulu Nchemba, Minister for Finance of Tanzania
a7157.speech: “In the 2025/26 financial year, the government expects to accelerate the growth of real GDP to 6.0 per cent in 2025, up from 5.5 per cent in 2024, to continue containing inflation and ensure it remains in the single-digit range of an average between 3.0 and 5.0 per cent in the medium term,” he explained.

a7157.speaker: Some Mwanza city residents interviewed by the Daily News
a7157.speech: Have expressed mixed reactions regarding the government’s budget, with some commending the government for presenting a budget that aims to address existing challenges while also implementing key national priorities.

a7157.speaker: Donald Kasongi, researcher from the Governance Links Institute
a7157.speech: Said this year’s government budget, which has increased by six trillion shillings from 50tr/- to 56tr/-, indicates that the government has raised the expectations of Tanzanians in financing social development activities in the country; further said the priorities in the budget are not clearly outlined, and that the Minister for Finance, Dr Mwigulu Nchemba, mentioned them in other areas. “It would have been better to clearly state our priorities so that we don’t end up trying to do everything everywhere,” he said.

a7157.speaker: Donald Kasongi, researcher from the Governance Links Institute
a7157.speech: Pointed out that a positive aspect of the budget is the reduced dependence on external aid, noting that out of the 56tr/-, only 1.4 trillion are allocated as aid from development partners. “This is a good sign that as a country we are reducing dependency on foreign aid. Even if we don’t receive that aid, we can still cover the shortfall,” he explained.

a7157.speaker: Donald Kasongi, researcher from the Governance Links Institute
a7157.speech: Regarding agriculture, said farmers need to work within a shorter period using the 10,000 tractors provided to cope with and adapt to climate change. “We should identify areas with high production potential even smallholder farmers so they can be reached and productivity in agriculture can be improved,” he said. ; On energy, noted that it was a heavily discussed topic in the government budget, particularly concerning forest protection through the use of clean cooking energy.

a7157.speaker: Donald Kasongi, researcher from the Governance Links Institute
a7157.speech: On the national debt, said 27 per cent of the budget going to debt repayment is a cautionary measure, adding that citizens are left questioning how the country will cope if the debt, which is currently at 40 per cent, approaches 50 per cent. “A quarter of the budget going to debt servicing is perhaps not a good sign. Another issue is employment, especially youth employment which seems to have been postponed. We should make efforts to attract youth by investing in agriculture,” he explained.

a7157.speaker: Mrs Christina Zegera, Bwiru Girls Secondary School Headmistress
a7157.speech: While commending the government for presenting a people-centred budget, said that in the education sector the budget has taken into account the need to ensure that every Tanzanian has access to quality education; said education is being delivered under a revised curriculum aimed at liberating people intellectually, economically and socially and that the budget increase meets expectations by aligning with established criteria; cited 2024 statistics showing the country currently has 20,533 primary schools, up from 3,270, with 229,840 teachers, up from 9,885 and 11,391,185 students, up from just 486,470, and in the secondary sector 6,269 schools, 128,686 teachers and 3,314,198 students.

a7273.speaker: EBSCO Information Services (press release signed by Briana Peters, Communications Specialist)
a7273.speech: Announced that Accra Technical University has been named one of four global recipients of the 2025 EBSCO Solar Grant, and that the EBSCO Solar initiative, now in its tenth year, awarded a total of $300,000 to support the installation of solar panels for public and private libraries across the globe, with ATU joining this year's recipients alongside Brooklyn Public Library, Patten Free Library and Wolfe County Public Library.

a7273.speaker: Accra Technical University spokesperson
a7273.speech: "We are aiming to locally generate between 60 to 75 per cent of our electricity needs," adding: "This grant brings us closer to achieving that goal, particularly in supporting critical academic infrastructure like the library."

a7456.speaker: Donald Trump, United States President
a7456.speech: Said his administration is accepting applications for his so-called "Trump Card", which promises applicants permanent residency for $5m ; "Thousands have been calling and asking how they can sign up to ride a beautiful road in gaining access to the Greatest Country and Market anywhere in the World," he said in a post on Truth Social. "It's called THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA. THE WAITING LIST IS NOW OPEN." ; first proposed the residency visa in February, saying his administration would offer wealthy applicants a "gold card" that grants residency and work rights as well as a path to citizenship: "They'll be wealthy, and they'll be successful, and they'll be spending a lot of money, and paying a lot of taxes and employing a lot of people."

a7456.speaker: Trump administration officials
a7456.speech: Have suggested that the card will replace the EB-5 immigrant investor visa programme, which grants permanent residency to immigrants who invest at least $1.05m in the US, or $800,000 in designated economically distressed areas.

a7456.speaker: Trump administration
a7456.speech: Has indicated there will be a vetting process, though it is unclear what criteria applicants may have to meet apart from the $5m price tag.
